content.english: ℣. O Lord, + open thou my lips.

content.latin: ℟. Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
content.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

segments.t: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Alleluia.

content.english: Ant. Jesus Christ, the King of kings * Come, let us adore!

content.latin: Ant. Iesum Christum, Regem regum: * Veníte adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Jesus Christ, the King of kings * Come, let us adore!

segments.t: Ant.
Iesum Christum, Regem regum: * Veníte adorémus.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Iesum Christum, Regem regum: * Veníte adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Jesus Christ, the King of kings * Come, let us adore!

segments.t: Ant.
Iesum Christum, Regem regum: * Veníte adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Come, let us adore!

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius
(genuflectitur)
veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

content.latin: Ant. Iesum Christum, Regem regum: * Veníte adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Jesus Christ, the King of kings * Come, let us adore!

segments.t: Ant.
Iesum Christum, Regem regum: * Veníte adorémus.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Come, let us adore!

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte adorémus.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Ant. Iesum Christum, Regem regum: * Veníte adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Jesus Christ, the King of kings * Come, let us adore!

content.latin: Ætérna Imago Altíssimi,
content.english: O thou eternal Image bright

content.latin: Lumen, Deus, de Lúmine,
content.english: Of God most high, thou Light of Light,

content.latin: Tibi, Redémptor glória,
content.english: To thee, Redeemer, glory be,

content.latin: Honor, potéstas régia.
content.english: And might and kingly majesty.

content.latin: Tu solus ante sǽcula
content.english: Sole hope of all created things,

content.latin: Spes atque centrum témporum,
content.english: Thou art the Lord and King of kings,

content.latin: Cui iure sceptrum géntium
content.english: Whom God, long ere creation's morn,

content.latin: Pater suprémum crédidit.
content.english: Had crowned to rule earth yet unborn.

content.latin: Tu flos pudícæ Vírginis,
content.english: Fair flower from the Virgin's breast,

content.latin: Nostræ caput propáginis,
content.english: Our race's Head for ever blest,

content.latin: Lapis cadúcus vértice
content.english: The stone that Daniel saw on high,

content.latin: Ac mole terras óccupans.
content.english: Which falling, o'er the world doth lie.

content.latin: Diro tyránno súbdita,
content.english: The race of men, condemned to lie

content.latin: Damnáta stirps mortálium,
content.english: Beneath the direful tyrant's yoke,

content.latin: Per te refrégit víncula
content.english: By thee at length the shackles broke

content.latin: Sibíque cælum víndicat.
content.english: And claimed the fatherland on high.

content.latin: Doctor, Sacérdos, Légifer
content.english: Priest, Teacher, Giver of the law,

content.latin: Præfers notátum sánguine
content.english: Thy Name the rapt Apostle saw

content.latin: In veste « Princeps príncipum
content.english: Writ on thy vesture and thy thigh:

content.latin: Regúmque Rex Altíssimus ».
content.english: The King Of Kings, The Lord Most High.

content.latin: Tibi voléntes súbdimur,
content.english: Fain would we own thy blessed sway,

content.latin: Qui iure cunctis ímperas:
content.english: Whose rule all creatures must obey;

content.latin: Hæc cívium beátitas
content.english: For happy is that state and throne

content.latin: Tuis subésse légibus.
content.english: Whose subjects seek thy will alone.

content.latin: Iesu, tibi sit glória,
content.english: All glory be, Jesu, to thee,

content.latin: Qui sceptra mundi témperas,
content.english: Thy scepter over all that be;

content.latin: Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
content.english: All glory, as is ever meet,

content.latin: In sempitérna sǽcula.
content.english: To Father and to Paraclete.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.english: Nocturn I

content.latin: Ant. Ego autem * constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, prǽdicans præcéptum eius.
content.english: Ant. I have been set up * as King by Him on Sion, His holy mountain, proclaiming His decree.

segments.t: Ant.
Ego autem * constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, prǽdicans præcéptum eius.

content.latin: Psalmus 2 [1]
content.english: Psalm 2 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 2

content.latin: 2:1 Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
content.english: 2:1 Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?

segments.t: Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?

content.latin: 2:2 Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.
content.english: 2:2 The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.

segments.t: Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.

content.latin: 2:3 Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.
content.english: 2:3 Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.

segments.t: Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.

content.latin: 2:4 Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
content.english: 2:4 He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.

segments.t: Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.

content.latin: 2:5 Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
content.english: 2:5 Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.

segments.t: Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.

content.latin: 2:6 Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.
content.english: 2:6 But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.

segments.t: Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.

content.latin: 2:7 Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
content.english: 2:7 The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.

segments.t: Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.

content.latin: 2:8 Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
content.english: 2:8 Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.

segments.t: Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.

content.latin: 2:9 Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
content.english: 2:9 Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

segments.t: Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.

content.latin: 2:10 Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.
content.english: 2:10 And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.

segments.t: Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.

content.latin: 2:11 Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
content.english: 2:11 Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.

segments.t: Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.

content.latin: 2:12 Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.
content.english: 2:12 Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.

segments.t: Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.

content.latin: 2:13 Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
content.english: 2:13 When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.

segments.t: Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Ant.
Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, prǽdicans præcéptum eius.

content.latin: Ant. Glória * et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine: ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius.
content.english: Ant. Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honor, O Lord, putting all things under His feet.

segments.t: Ant.
Glória * et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine: ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius.

content.latin: Psalmus 8 [2]
content.english: Psalm 8 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 8

content.latin: 8:2 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:2 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.latin: 8:2 Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.
content.english: 8:2 For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.

segments.t: Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.

content.latin: 8:3 Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
content.english: 8:3 Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.

segments.t: Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.

content.latin: 8:4 Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
content.english: 8:4 For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.

segments.t: Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.

content.latin: 8:5 Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
content.english: 8:5 What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?

segments.t: Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?

content.latin: 8:6 Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
content.english: 8:6 Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * and hast set him over the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.

content.latin: 8:8 Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
content.english: 8:8 Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.

segments.t: Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.

content.latin: 8:9 Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.
content.english: 8:9 The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, * that pass through the paths of the sea.

segments.t: Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.

content.latin: 8:10 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:10 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in all the earth!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Glória et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine: ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius.
content.english: Ant. Thou hast crowned him with glory and honor, O Lord, putting all things under His feet.

segments.t: Ant.
Glória et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine: ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius.

content.latin: Ant. Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: Ant. Reach up * you ancient portals, that the King of glory may come in.

segments.t: Ant.
Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: Psalmus 23 [3]
content.english: Psalm 23 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 23

content.latin: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
content.english: 23:1 The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.

segments.t: Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.

content.latin: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
content.english: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

segments.t: Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.

content.latin: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?
content.english: 23:3 Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?

segments.t: Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?

content.latin: 23:4 Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.
content.english: 23:4 The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

segments.t: Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.

content.latin: 23:5 Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
content.english: 23:5 He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.

segments.t: Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.

content.latin: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.
content.english: 23:6 This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

segments.t: Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.

content.latin: 23:7 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:7 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

segments.t: Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: 23:8 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
content.english: 23:8 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.

segments.t: Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.

content.latin: 23:9 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:9 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

segments.t: Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: 23:10 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:10 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.

segments.t: Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Elevámini, portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: Ant. Reach up you ancient portals, that the King of glory may come in.

segments.t: Ant.
Elevámini, portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: ℣. Data est mihi omnis potéstas.
content.english: ℣. All power has been given to me.

segments.t: Data est mihi omnis potéstas.

content.latin: ℟. In cælo et in terra.
content.english: ℟. In heaven and on earth.

segments.t: In cælo et in terra.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: De Epistola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Colossénses
content.english: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Colossians

content.latin: 3 Grátias agimus Deo, et Patri Dómini nostri Iesu Christi, semper pro vobis orántes,
content.english: 3 Grace be to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ. We give thanks to God, and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you.

segments.t: Grátias agimus Deo, et Patri Dómini nostri Iesu Christi, semper pro vobis orántes,

content.latin: 4 Audiéntes fidem vestram in Christo Iesu, et dilectiónem quam habétis in sanctos omnes,
content.english: 4 Hearing your faith in Christ Jesus, and the love which you have towards all the saints.

segments.t: Audiéntes fidem vestram in Christo Iesu, et dilectiónem quam habétis in sanctos omnes,

content.latin: 5 Propter spem, quæ repósita est vobis in cælis, quam audístis in verbo veritátis Evangélii,
content.english: 5 For the hope that is laid up for you in heaven, which you have heard in the word of the truth of the gospel,

segments.t: Propter spem, quæ repósita est vobis in cælis, quam audístis in verbo veritátis Evangélii,

content.latin: 6 Quod pervénit ad vos, sicut et in univérso mundo est, et fructíficat, et crescit, sicut in vobis, ex ea die, qua audístis, et cognovístis grátiam Dei in veritáte,
content.english: 6 Which is come unto you, as also it is in the whole world, and bringeth forth fruit and groweth, even as it doth in you, since the day you heard and knew the grace of God in truth.

segments.t: Quod pervénit ad vos, sicut et in univérso mundo est, et fructíficat, et crescit, sicut in vobis, ex ea die, qua audístis, et cognovístis grátiam Dei in veritáte,

content.latin: 7 Sicut didicístis ab Epáphra, caríssimo consérvo nostro, qui est fidélis pro vobis miníster Christi Iesu,
content.english: 7 As you learned of Epaphras, our most beloved fellow servant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ Jesus;

segments.t: Sicut didicístis ab Epáphra, caríssimo consérvo nostro, qui est fidélis pro vobis miníster Christi Iesu,

content.latin: 8 Qui étiam manifestávit nobis dilectiónem vestram in spíritu.
content.english: 8 Who also hath manifested to us your love in the spirit.

segments.t: Qui étiam manifestávit nobis dilectiónem vestram in spíritu.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Super sólium David et super regnum eius sedébit in ætérnum:
content.english: ℟. He shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom forever.

segments.t: Super sólium David et super regnum eius sedébit in ætérnum:

content.latin: * Et vocábitur nomen eius Deus, Fortis, Princeps pacis.
content.english: * And His name shall be called God, the Mighty, the Prince of peace.

content.latin: ℣. Multiplicábitur eius impérium, et pacis non erit finis.
content.english: ℣. His dominion is vast and forever peaceful.

segments.t: Multiplicábitur eius impérium, et pacis non erit finis.

content.latin: ℟. Et vocábitur nomen eius Deus, Fortis, Princeps pacis.
content.english: ℟. And His name shall be called God, the Mighty, the Prince of peace.

segments.t: Et vocábitur nomen eius Deus, Fortis, Princeps pacis.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 9 Ideo et nos ex qua die audívimus, non cessámus pro vobis orántes, et postulántes ut impleámini agnitióne voluntátis eius, in omni sapiéntia et intelléctu spiritáli;
content.english: 9 Therefore we also, from the day that we heard it, cease not to pray for you, and to beg that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom, and spiritual understanding:

segments.t: Ideo et nos ex qua die audívimus, non cessámus pro vobis orántes, et postulántes ut impleámini agnitióne voluntátis eius, in omni sapiéntia et intelléctu spiritáli;

content.latin: 10 Ut ambulétis digne Deo per ómnia placéntes; in omni ópere bono fructificántes, et crescéntes in sciéntia Dei:
content.english: 10 That you may walk worthy of God, in all things pleasing; being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God:

segments.t: Ut ambulétis digne Deo per ómnia placéntes; in omni ópere bono fructificántes, et crescéntes in sciéntia Dei:

content.latin: 11 In omni virtúte confortáti secúndum poténtiam claritátis eius, in omni patiéntia et longanimitáte cum gáudio;
content.english: 11 Strengthened with all might, according to the power of his glory, in all patience and longsuffering with joy,

segments.t: In omni virtúte confortáti secúndum poténtiam claritátis eius, in omni patiéntia et longanimitáte cum gáudio;

content.latin: 12 Grátias agéntes Deo Patri, qui dignos nos fecit in partem sortis sanctórum in lúmine,
content.english: 12 Giving thanks to God the Father, who hath made us worthy to be partakers of the lot of the saints in light:

segments.t: Grátias agéntes Deo Patri, qui dignos nos fecit in partem sortis sanctórum in lúmine,

content.latin: 13 Qui erípuit nos de potestáte tenebrárum, et tránstulit in regnum Fílii dilectiónis suæ,
content.english: 13 Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love,

segments.t: Qui erípuit nos de potestáte tenebrárum, et tránstulit in regnum Fílii dilectiónis suæ,

content.latin: 14 In quo habémus redemptiónem per sánguinem eius, remissiónem peccatórum.
content.english: 14 In whom we have redemption through his blood, the remission of sins;

segments.t: In quo habémus redemptiónem per sánguinem eius, remissiónem peccatórum.

content.latin: 15 Qui est imágo Dei invisíbilis, primogénitus omnis creatúræ;
content.english: 15 Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature:

segments.t: Qui est imágo Dei invisíbilis, primogénitus omnis creatúræ;

content.latin: 16 Quóniam in ipso cóndita sunt univérsa in cælis et in terra, visibília, et invisibília, sive Throni, sive Dominatiónes, sive Principátus, sive Potestátes: ómnia per ipsum et in ipso creáta sunt:
content.english: 16 For in him were all things created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones, or dominations, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him and in him.

segments.t: Quóniam in ipso cóndita sunt univérsa in cælis et in terra, visibília, et invisibília, sive Throni, sive Dominatiónes, sive Principátus, sive Potestátes: ómnia per ipsum et in ipso creáta sunt:

content.latin: 17 Et ipse est ante omnes, et ómnia in ipso constant.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Et ipse est ante omnes, et ómnia in ipso constant.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. In the vision during the night I saw the Son of man coming on the clouds of heaven; and He was given kingship and glory.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Aspiciébam in visu noctis, et ecce in núbibus cæli Fílius hóminis veniébat: et datum est ei regnum et honor:
content.english: * Nations and people of every language serve Him.

segments.t: Aspiciébam in visu noctis, et ecce in núbibus cæli Fílius hóminis veniébat: et datum est ei regnum et honor:

content.latin: * Et omnis pópulus, tribus et linguæ sérvient ei.
content.english: ℣. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that shall not be taken away, His kingship shall not be destroyed.

content.latin: ℣. Potéstas eius, potéstas ætérna, quæ non auferétur: et regnum eius, quod non corrumpétur.
content.english: ℟. Nations and people of every language serve Him.

segments.t: Potéstas eius, potéstas ætérna, quæ non auferétur: et regnum eius, quod non corrumpétur.

content.latin: ℟. Et omnis pópulus, tribus et linguæ sérvient ei.

segments.t: Et omnis pópulus, tribus et linguæ sérvient ei.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 18 Et ipse est caput córporis Ecclésiæ, qui est princípium, primogénitus ex mórtuis, ut sit in ómnibus ipse primátum tenens;
content.english: And he is before all, and by him all things consist.

segments.t: Et ipse est caput córporis Ecclésiæ, qui est princípium, primogénitus ex mórtuis, ut sit in ómnibus ipse primátum tenens;

content.latin: 19 Quia in ipso complácuit omnem plenitúdinem inhabitáre,
content.english: And he is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he may hold the primacy:

segments.t: Quia in ipso complácuit omnem plenitúdinem inhabitáre,

content.latin: 20 Et per eum reconciliáre ómnia in ipsum, pacíficans per sánguinem crucis eius, sive quæ in terris, sive quæ in cælis sunt.
content.english: Because in him, it hath well pleased the Father, that all fullness should dwell;

segments.t: Et per eum reconciliáre ómnia in ipsum, pacíficans per sánguinem crucis eius, sive quæ in terris, sive quæ in cælis sunt.

content.latin: 21 Et vos, cum essétis aliquándo alienáti, et inimíci sensu in opéribus malis;
content.english: And through him to reconcile all things unto himself, making peace through the blood of his cross, both as to the things that are on earth, and the things that are in heaven.

segments.t: Et vos, cum essétis aliquándo alienáti, et inimíci sensu in opéribus malis;

content.latin: 22 Nunc autem reconciliávit in córpore carnis eius per mortem, exhibére vos sanctos, et immaculátos, et irreprehensíbiles coram ipso;
content.english: And you, whereas you were some time alienated and enemies in mind in evil works:

segments.t: Nunc autem reconciliávit in córpore carnis eius per mortem, exhibére vos sanctos, et immaculátos, et irreprehensíbiles coram ipso;

content.latin: 23 Si tamen permanétis in fide fundáti, et stábiles, et immóbiles a spe evangélii, quod audístis, quod prædicátum est in univérsa creatúra quæ sub cælo est, cuius factus sum ego Paulus miníster.
content.english: Yet now he hath reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unspotted, and blameless before him:

segments.t: Si tamen permanétis in fide fundáti, et stábiles, et immóbiles a spe evangélii, quod audístis, quod prædicátum est in univérsa creatúra quæ sub cælo est, cuius factus sum ego Paulus miníster.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: If so ye continue in the faith, grounded and settled, and immoveable from the hope of the gospel which you have heard, which is preached in all the creation that is under heaven, whereof I, Paul, am made a minister.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Tu Béthlehem Ephrata, párvulus in míllibus Iuda: ex te mihi egrediétur qui sit dominátor in Israël:
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Tu Béthlehem Ephrata, párvulus in míllibus Iuda: ex te mihi egrediétur qui sit dominátor in Israël:

content.latin: * Et erit iste Pax.
content.english: ℟. You, Bethlehem-Ephrata, too small among the clans of Juda, from you shall come forth for Me one who is to be ruler in Israel;

content.latin: ℣. Egréssus eius ab inítio, a diébus æternitátis: stabit, et pascet in fortitúdine Dómini.
content.english: * And He shall be Peace.

segments.t: Egréssus eius ab inítio, a diébus æternitátis: stabit, et pascet in fortitúdine Dómini.

content.latin: ℟. Et erit iste Pax.
content.english: ℣. His origin is from old, from ancient times. He shall stand firm and shepherd his flock by the strength of the Lord.

segments.t: Et erit iste Pax.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℟. And He shall be Peace.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Et erit iste Pax.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Et erit iste Pax.

content.english: ℟. And He shall be Peace.

content.latin: Nocturnus II
content.english: Nocturn II

segments.t: Nocturnus II

content.latin: Ant. Sedébit * Dóminus Rex in ætérnum: Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.
content.english: Ant. The Lord is enthroned * as King forever; may the Lord bless his people with peace.

segments.t: Ant.
Sedébit * Dóminus Rex in ætérnum: Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.

content.latin: Psalmus 28 [4]
content.english: Psalm 28 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 28

content.latin: 28:1 Afférte Dómino, fílii Dei: * afférte Dómino fílios aríetum.
content.english: 28:1 Bring to the Lord, O ye children of God: * bring to the Lord the offspring of rams.

segments.t: Afférte Dómino, fílii Dei: * afférte Dómino fílios aríetum.

content.latin: 28:2 Afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem, afférte Dómino glóriam nómini eius: * adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto eius.
content.english: 28:2 Bring to the Lord glory and honour: bring to the Lord glory to his name: * adore ye the Lord in his holy court.

segments.t: Afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem, afférte Dómino glóriam nómini eius: * adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto eius.

content.latin: 28:3 Vox Dómini super aquas, Deus maiestátis intónuit: * Dóminus super aquas multas.
content.english: 28:3 The voice of the Lord is upon the waters; the God of majesty hath thundered, * The Lord is upon many waters.

segments.t: Vox Dómini super aquas, Deus maiestátis intónuit: * Dóminus super aquas multas.

content.latin: 28:4 Vox Dómini in virtúte: * vox Dómini in magnificéntia.
content.english: 28:4 The voice of the Lord is in power; * the voice of the Lord in magnificence.

segments.t: Vox Dómini in virtúte: * vox Dómini in magnificéntia.

content.latin: 28:5 Vox Dómini confringéntis cedros: * et confrínget Dóminus cedros Líbani:
content.english: 28:5 The voice of the Lord breaketh the cedars: * yea, the Lord shall break the cedars of Libanus.

segments.t: Vox Dómini confringéntis cedros: * et confrínget Dóminus cedros Líbani:

content.latin: 28:6 Et commínuet eas tamquam vítulum Líbani: * et diléctus quemádmodum fílius unicórnium.
content.english: 28:6 And shall reduce them to pieces, as a calf of Libanus, * and as the beloved son of unicorns.

segments.t: Et commínuet eas tamquam vítulum Líbani: * et diléctus quemádmodum fílius unicórnium.

content.latin: 28:7 Vox Dómini intercidéntis flammam ignis: * vox Dómini concutiéntis desértum: et commovébit Dóminus desértum Cades.
content.english: 28:7 The voice of the Lord divideth the flame of fire: * The voice of the Lord shaketh the desert: and the Lord shall shake the desert of Cades.

segments.t: Vox Dómini intercidéntis flammam ignis: * vox Dómini concutiéntis desértum: et commovébit Dóminus desértum Cades.

content.latin: 28:9 Vox Dómini præparántis cervos, et revelábit condénsa: * et in templo eius omnes dicent glóriam.
content.english: 28:9 The voice of the Lord prepareth the stags: and he will discover the thick woods: * and in his temple all shall speak his glory.

segments.t: Vox Dómini præparántis cervos, et revelábit condénsa: * et in templo eius omnes dicent glóriam.

content.latin: 28:10 Dóminus dilúvium inhabitáre facit: * et sedébit Dóminus Rex in ætérnum.
content.english: 28:10 The Lord maketh the flood to dwell: * and the Lord shall sit king for ever.

segments.t: Dóminus dilúvium inhabitáre facit: * et sedébit Dóminus Rex in ætérnum.

content.latin: 28:11 Dóminus virtútem pópulo suo dabit: * Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.
content.english: 28:11 The Lord will give strength to his people: * the Lord will bless his people with peace.

segments.t: Dóminus virtútem pópulo suo dabit: * Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Sedébit Dóminus Rex in ætérnum: Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.
content.english: Ant. The Lord is enthroned as King forever; may the Lord bless his people with peace.

segments.t: Ant.
Sedébit Dóminus Rex in ætérnum: Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.

content.latin: Ant. Virga directiónis, * virga regni tui: proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: Ant. A tempered rod * is thy royal scepter; therefore shall nations praise thee forever and ever.

segments.t: Ant.
Virga directiónis, * virga regni tui: proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: Psalmus 44 [5]
content.english: Psalm 44 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 44

content.latin: 44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

segments.t: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

segments.t: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

segments.t: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

segments.t: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

content.latin: Cum Annus sacer non unam ad illustrándum Christi regnum habúerit opportunitátem, vidémur rem factúri Apostólico múneri in primis consentáneam, si, plurimórum Patrum Cardinálium, Episcopórum fideliúmque précibus, ad Nos aut singillátim aut commúniter delátis, concedéntes, hunc ipsum Annum peculiári festo Dómini Nostri Iesu Christi Regis in ecclesiásticam liturgíam inducéndo clausérimus. Ut transláta verbi significatióne Rex appellarétur Christus ob summum excelléntiæ gradum, quo inter omnes res creátas præstat atque éminet, iam diu communitérque usu venit. Ita enim fit, ut regnare is « in méntibus hóminum » dicátur non tam ob mentis áciem scientiǽque suæ amplitúdinem, quam quod ipse est Véritas, et veritátem ab eo mortáles hauríre atque obediénter accípere necésse est; « in voluntátibus » item « hóminum », quia non modo sanctitáti in eo voluntátis divínæ perfécta prorsus respóndet humánæ intégritas atque obtemperátio, sed étiam líberæ voluntáti nostræ id permotióne instinctúque suo súbicit, unde ad nobilíssima quæque exardescámus. « Córdium » dénique « Rex » Christus agnóscitur ob eius « supereminéntem sciéntiæ caritátem » et mansuetúdinem benignitatémque ánimos alliciéntem: nec enim quemquam usque ádeo ab universitáte géntium, ut Christum Iesum, aut amári aliquándo cóntigit aut amátum iri in pósterum contínget. Verum, ut rem préssius ingrediámur, nemo non videt, nomen potestatémque regis, própria quidem verbi significatióne, Christo hómini vindicári oportére; nam, nisi quátenus homo est, a Patre « potestátem et honórem et regnum » accepísse dici nequit, quandóquidem Dei Verbum, cui éadem est cum Patre substántia, non potest ómnia cum Patre non habére commúnia, proptereáque ipsum in res creátas univérsas summum atque absolutíssimum impérium.
content.english: Since this Holy Year therefore has provided more than one opportunity to enhance the glory of the kingdom of Christ, we deem it in keeping with our Apostolic office to accede to the desire of many of the Cardinals, Bishops, and faithful, made known to Us both individually and collectively, by closing this Holy Year with the insertion into the Sacred Liturgy of a special feast of the Kingship of Our Lord Jesus Christ. This matter is so dear to Our heart, Venerable Brethren, that I would wish to address to you a few words concerning it. It will be for you later to explain in a manner suited to the understanding of the faithful what We are about to say concerning the Kingship of Christ, so that the annual feast which We shall decree may be attended with much fruit and produce beneficial results in the future. It has long been a common custom to give to Christ the metaphorical title of “King,” because of the high degree of perfection whereby he excels all creatures. So he is said to reign “in the hearts of men,” both by reason of the keenness of his intellect and the extent of his knowledge, and also because he is very truth, and it is from him that truth must be obediently received by all mankind. He reigns, too, in the wills of men, for in him the human will was perfectly and entirely obedient to the Holy Will of God, and further by his grace and inspiration he so subjects our free-will as to incite us to the most noble endeavors. He is King of hearts, too, by reason of his “charity which exceedeth all knowledge.” And his mercy and kindness which draw all men to him, for never has it been known, nor will it ever be, that man be loved so much and so universally as Jesus Christ. But if we ponder this matter more deeply, we cannot but see that the title and the power of King belongs to Christ as man in the strict and proper sense too. For it is only as man that he may be said to have received from the Father “power and glory and a kingdom,” since the Word of God, as consubstantial with the Father, has all things in common with him, and therefore has necessarily supreme and absolute dominion over all things created.

content.latin: Quo autem hæc Dómini nostri dígnitas et potéstas fundaménto consístat, apte Cyríllus Alexandrínus animadvértit: « Omnium, ut verbo dicam, creaturárum dominátum óbtinet, non per vim extórtum, nec aliúnde invéctum, sed esséntia sua et natúra »; scílicet eius principátus illa nítitur unióne mirábili, quam hypostáticam appéllant. Unde conséquitur, non modo ut Christus ab Angelis et homínibus Deus sit adorándus, sed étiam ut eius império Hóminis, Angeli et hómines páreant et subiécti sint: nempe ut vel solo hypostáticæ uniónis nómine Christus potestátem in univérsas creatúras obtíneat. Iamvéro, ut huius vim et natúram principátus paucis declarémus, dícere vix áttinet tríplici eum potestáte continéri, qua si carúerit, principátus vix intellégitur. Id ipsum deprómpta atque alláta ex sacris Lítteris de universáli Redemptóris nostri império testimónia plus quam satis signíficant, atque est cathólica fide credéndum, Christum Iesum homínibus datum esse útique Redemptórem cui fidant, at una simul legislatórem cui obédiant. Ipsum autem evangélia non tam leges condidísse narrant, quam leges condéntem indúcunt: quæ quidem præcépta quicúmque servárint, iídem a divíno Magístro, álias áliis verbis, et suam in eum caritátem probatúri et in dilectióne eius mansúri dicúntur. Iudiciáriam vero potestátem sibi a Patre attribútam ipse Iesus Iudǽis, de Sábbati requiéte per mirábilem débilis hóminis sanatiónem violáta criminántibus, denúntiat: « Neque enim Pater iúdicat quemquam, sed omne iudícium dedit Fílio ». In quo id étiam comprehénditur (quóniam res a iudício disiúngi nequit) ut prǽmia et pœnas homínibus adhuc vivéntibus iure suo déferat. At prætérea potéstas illa, quam exsecutiónis vocant, Christo adiudicánda est, útpote cuius império parére omnes necésse sit, et ea quidem denuntiáta contumácibus irrogatióne suppliciórum, quæ nemo possit effúgere.
content.english: The foundation of this power and dignity of Our Lord is rightly indicated by Cyril of Alexandria. “Christ,” he says, “has dominion over all creatures, a dominion not seized by violence nor usurped, but his by essence and by nature.” His kingship is founded upon the ineffable hypostatic union. From this it follows not only that Christ is to be adored by angels and men, but that to him as man angels and men are subject, and must recognize his empire; by reason of the hypostatic union Christ has power over all creatures. But a thought that must give us even greater joy and consolation is this that Christ is our King by acquired, as well as by natural right, for he is our Redeemer. Would that they who forget what they have cost their Saviour might recall the words: “You were not redeemed with corruptible things, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb unspotted and undefiled.” We are no longer our own property, for Christ has purchased us “with a great price”; our very bodies are the “members of Christ.” Let Us explain briefly the nature and meaning of this lordship of Christ. It consists, We need scarcely say, in a threefold power which is essential to lordship. This is sufficiently clear from the scriptural testimony already adduced concerning the universal dominion of our Redeemer, and moreover it is a dogma of faith that Jesus Christ was given to man, not only as our Redeemer, but also as a law-giver, to whom obedience is due. Not only do the gospels tell us that he made laws, but they present him to us in the act of making them. Those who keep them show their love for their Divine Master, and he promises that they shall remain in his love. He claimed judicial power as received from his Father, when the Jews accused him of breaking the Sabbath by the miraculous cure of a sick man. “For neither doth the Father judge any man; but hath given all judgment to the Son.” In this power is included the right of rewarding and punishing all men living, for this right is inseparable from that of judging. Executive power, too, belongs to Christ, for all must obey his commands; none may escape them, nor the sanctions he has imposed.

content.latin: Verúmtamen eiúsmodi regnum præcípuo quodam modo et spirituále esse et ad spirituália pertinére, cum ea, quæ ex Bíbliis supra protúlimus, verba planíssime osténdunt, tum Christus Dóminus sua agéndi ratióne confírmat. Síquidem, non una data occasióne, cum Iudǽi, immo vel ipsi Apóstoli, per errórem censérent, fore ut Messías pópulum in libertátem vindicáret regnúmque Israël restitúeret, vanam ipse opiniónem ac spem adímere et convéllere; rex a circumfúsa admirántium multitúdine renuntiándus, et nomen et honórem fugiéndo latendóque detrectáre; coram prǽside Románo edícere, regnum suum « de hoc mundo » non esse. Quod quidem regnum tale in evangéliis propónitur, in quod hómines pœniténtiam agéndo íngredi parent, íngredi vero néqueant nisi per fidem et baptísmum, qui etsi est ritus extérnus, interiórem tamen regeneratiónem signíficat atque éfficit; oppónitur únice regno Sátanæ et potestáti tenebrárum, et ab ásseclis póstulat, non solum ut, abalienáto a divítiis rebúsque terrénis ánimo, morum prǽferant lenitátem et esúriant sitiántque iustítiam, sed étiam ut semetípsos ábnegent et crucem suam tollant. Cum autem Christus et Ecclésiam Redémptor sánguine suo acquisíverit et Sacérdos se ipse pro peccátis hóstiam obtúlerit perpetuóque ófferat, cui non videátur régium ipsum munus utriúsque illíus natúram múneris indúere ac participáre? Túrpiter, ceteróquin, erret, qui a Christo hómine rerum civílium quarúmlibet impérium abiúdicet, cum is a Patre ius in res creátas absolutíssimum sic obtíneat, ut ómnia in suo arbítrio sint pósita. Itaque, auctoritáte Nostra apostólica, festum Dómini Nostri Iesu Christi Regis institúimus, quotánnis, postrémo mensis octóbris domínico die, qui scílicet Omnium Sanctórum celebritátem próxime antecédit, ubíque terrárum agéndum. Item præcípimus, ut eo ipso die géneris humáni Sacratíssimo Cordi Iesu dedicátio quotánnis renovétur.
content.english: This kingdom is spiritual and is concerned with spiritual things. That this is so the above quotations from Scripture amply prove, and Christ by his own action confirms it. On many occasions, when the Jews and even the Apostles wrongly supposed that the Messiah would restore the liberties and the kingdom of Israel, he repelled and denied such a suggestion. When the populace thronged around him in admiration and would have acclaimed him King, he shrank from the honor and sought safety in flight. Before the Roman magistrate he declared that his kingdom was not of this world. The gospels present this kingdom as one which men prepare to enter by penance, and cannot actually enter except by faith and by baptism, which, though an external rite, signifies and produces an interior regeneration. This kingdom is opposed to none other than to that of Satan and to the power of darkness. It demands of its subjects a spirit of detachment from riches and earthly things, and a spirit of gentleness. They must hunger and thirst after justice, and more than this, they must deny themselves and carry the cross. Christ as our Redeemer purchased the Church at the price of his own blood; as priest he offered himself, and continues to offer himself as a victim for our sins. Is it not evident, then, that his kingly dignity partakes in a manner of both these offices? It would be a grave error, on the other hand, to say that Christ has no authority whatever in civil affairs, since, by virtue of the absolute empire over all creatures committed to him by the Father, all things are in his power. Therefore by Our Apostolic Authority We institute the Feast of the Kingship of Our Lord Jesus Christ to be observed yearly throughout the whole world on the last Sunday of the month of October - the Sunday, that is, which immediately precedes the Feast of All Saints. We further ordain that the dedication of mankind to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, to be renewed yearly.

content.latin: Psalmus 71 [7]
content.english: Psalm 71 [7]

segments.t: Psalmus 71

content.latin: 71:2 Deus, iudícium tuum regi da: * et iustítiam tuam fílio regis:
content.english: 71:2 Give to the king thy judgment, O God: * and to the king’s son thy justice:

segments.t: Deus, iudícium tuum regi da: * et iustítiam tuam fílio regis:

content.latin: 71:2 Iudicáre pópulum tuum in iustítia, * et páuperes tuos in iudício.
content.english: 71:2 To judge thy people with justice, * and thy poor with judgment.

segments.t: Iudicáre pópulum tuum in iustítia, * et páuperes tuos in iudício.

content.latin: 71:3 Suscípiant montes pacem pópulo: * et colles iustítiam.
content.english: 71:3 Let the mountains receive peace for the people: * and the hills justice.

segments.t: Suscípiant montes pacem pópulo: * et colles iustítiam.

content.latin: 71:4 Iudicábit páuperes pópuli, et salvos fáciet fílios páuperum: * et humiliábit calumniatórem.
content.english: 71:4 He shall judge the poor of the people, and he shall save the children of the poor: * and he shall humble the oppressor.

segments.t: Iudicábit páuperes pópuli, et salvos fáciet fílios páuperum: * et humiliábit calumniatórem.

content.latin: 71:5 Et permanébit cum sole, et ante lunam, * in generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 71:5 And he shall continue with the sun, and before the moon, * throughout all generations.

segments.t: Et permanébit cum sole, et ante lunam, * in generatióne et generatiónem.

content.latin: 71:6 Descéndet sicut plúvia in vellus: * et sicut stillicídia stillántia super terram.
content.english: 71:6 He shall come down like rain upon the fleece; * and as showers falling gently upon the earth.

segments.t: Descéndet sicut plúvia in vellus: * et sicut stillicídia stillántia super terram.

content.latin: 71:7 Oriétur in diébus eius iustítia, et abundántia pacis: * donec auferátur luna.
content.english: 71:7 In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace, * till the moon be taken away.

segments.t: Oriétur in diébus eius iustítia, et abundántia pacis: * donec auferátur luna.

content.latin: 71:8 Et dominábitur a mari usque ad mare: * et a flúmine usque ad términos orbis terrárum.
content.english: 71:8 And he shall rule from sea to sea, * and from the river unto the ends of the earth.

segments.t: Et dominábitur a mari usque ad mare: * et a flúmine usque ad términos orbis terrárum.

content.latin: 71:9 Coram illo prócident Æthíopes: * et inimíci eius terram lingent.
content.english: 71:9 Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down: * and his enemies shall lick the ground.

segments.t: Coram illo prócident Æthíopes: * et inimíci eius terram lingent.

content.latin: 71:10 Reges Tharsis, et ínsulæ múnera ófferent: * reges Árabum et Saba dona addúcent.
content.english: 71:10 The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall offer presents: * the kings of the Arabians and of Saba shall bring gifts:

segments.t: Reges Tharsis, et ínsulæ múnera ófferent: * reges Árabum et Saba dona addúcent.

content.latin: 71:11 Et adorábunt eum omnes reges terræ: * omnes gentes sérvient ei:
content.english: 71:11 And all kings of the earth shall adore him: * all nations shall serve him.

segments.t: Et adorábunt eum omnes reges terræ: * omnes gentes sérvient ei:

content.latin: 71:12 Quia liberábit páuperem a poténte: * et páuperem, cui non erat adiútor.
content.english: 71:12 For he shall deliver the poor from the mighty: * and the needy that had no helper.

segments.t: Quia liberábit páuperem a poténte: * et páuperem, cui non erat adiútor.

content.latin: 71:13 Parcet páuperi et ínopi: * et ánimas páuperum salvas fáciet.
content.english: 71:13 He shall spare the poor and needy: * and he shall save the souls of the poor.

segments.t: Parcet páuperi et ínopi: * et ánimas páuperum salvas fáciet.

content.latin: 71:14 Ex usúris et iniquitáte rédimet ánimas eórum: * et honorábile nomen eórum coram illo.
content.english: 71:14 He shall redeem their souls from usuries and iniquity: * and their names shall be honourable in his sight.

segments.t: Ex usúris et iniquitáte rédimet ánimas eórum: * et honorábile nomen eórum coram illo.

content.latin: 71:15 Et vivet, et dábitur ei de auro Arábiæ, et adorábunt de ipso semper: * tota die benedícent ei.
content.english: 71:15 And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Arabia, for him they shall always adore: * they shall bless him all the day.

segments.t: Et vivet, et dábitur ei de auro Arábiæ, et adorábunt de ipso semper: * tota die benedícent ei.

content.latin: 71:16 Et erit firmaméntum in terra in summis móntium, superextollétur super Líbanum fructus eius: * et florébunt de civitáte sicut fænum terræ.
content.english: 71:16 And there shall be a firmament on the earth on the tops of mountains, above Libanus shall the fruit thereof be exalted: * and they of the city shall flourish like the grass of the earth.

segments.t: Et erit firmaméntum in terra in summis móntium, superextollétur super Líbanum fructus eius: * et florébunt de civitáte sicut fænum terræ.

content.latin: 71:17 Sit nomen eius benedíctum in sǽcula: * ante solem pérmanet nomen eius.
content.english: 71:17 Let his name be blessed for evermore: * his name continueth before the sun.

segments.t: Sit nomen eius benedíctum in sǽcula: * ante solem pérmanet nomen eius.

content.latin: 71:17 Et benedicéntur in ipso omnes tribus terræ: * omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.
content.english: 71:17 And in him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed: * all nations shall magnify him.

segments.t: Et benedicéntur in ipso omnes tribus terræ: * omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.

content.latin: 71:18 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, * qui facit mirabília solus:
content.english: 71:18 Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, * who alone doth wonderful things.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, * qui facit mirabília solus:

content.latin: 71:19 Et benedíctum nomen maiestátis eius in ætérnum: * et replébitur maiestáte eius omnis terra: fiat, fiat.
content.english: 71:19 And blessed be the name of his majesty for ever: * and the whole earth shall be filled with his majesty. So be it. So be it.

segments.t: Et benedíctum nomen maiestátis eius in ætérnum: * et replébitur maiestáte eius omnis terra: fiat, fiat.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Benedicéntur in ipso omnes tribus terræ; omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.
content.english: Ant. In Him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed; all the nations shall proclaim His greatness.

Benedicéntur in ipso omnes tribus terræ; omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.

Psalmus 88(2-30)

content.latin: 88:2 Misericórdias Dómini * in ætérnum cantábo.
content.english: 88:2 The mercies of the Lord * I will sing for ever.

segments.t: Misericórdias Dómini * in ætérnum cantábo.

content.latin: 88:2 In generatiónem et generatiónem * annuntiábo veritátem tuam in ore meo.
content.english: 88:2 I will shew forth thy truth with my mouth * to generation and generation.

segments.t: In generatiónem et generatiónem * annuntiábo veritátem tuam in ore meo.

content.latin: 88:3 Quóniam dixísti: In ætérnum misericórdia ædificábitur in cælis: * præparábitur véritas tua in eis.
content.english: 88:3 For thou hast said: Mercy shall be built up for ever in the heavens: * thy truth shall be prepared in them.

segments.t: Quóniam dixísti: In ætérnum misericórdia ædificábitur in cælis: * præparábitur véritas tua in eis.

content.latin: 88:4 Dispósui testaméntum eléctis meis, iurávi David, servo meo: * Usque in ætérnum præparábo semen tuum.
content.english: 88:4 I have made a covenant with my elect: I have sworn to David my servant: * Thy seed will I settle for ever.

segments.t: Dispósui testaméntum eléctis meis, iurávi David, servo meo: * Usque in ætérnum præparábo semen tuum.

content.latin: 88:5 Et ædificábo in generatiónem et generatiónem * sedem tuam.
content.english: 88:5 And I will build up thy throne * unto generation and generation.

segments.t: Et ædificábo in generatiónem et generatiónem * sedem tuam.

content.latin: 88:6 Confitebúntur cæli mirabília tua, Dómine: * étenim veritátem tuam in ecclésia sanctórum.
content.english: 88:6 The heavens shall confess thy wonders, O Lord: * and thy truth in the church of the saints.

segments.t: Confitebúntur cæli mirabília tua, Dómine: * étenim veritátem tuam in ecclésia sanctórum.

content.latin: 88:7 Quóniam quis in núbibus æquábitur Dómino: * símilis erit Deo in fíliis Dei?
content.english: 88:7 For who in the clouds can be compared to the Lord: * or who among the sons of God shall be like to God?

segments.t: Quóniam quis in núbibus æquábitur Dómino: * símilis erit Deo in fíliis Dei?

content.latin: 88:8 Deus, qui glorificátur in consílio sanctórum: * magnus et terríbilis super omnes qui in circúitu eius sunt.
content.english: 88:8 God, who is glorified in the assembly of the saints: * great and terrible above all them that are about him.

segments.t: Deus, qui glorificátur in consílio sanctórum: * magnus et terríbilis super omnes qui in circúitu eius sunt.

content.latin: 88:9 Dómine, Deus virtútum, quis símilis tibi? * potens es, Dómine, et véritas tua in circúitu tuo.
content.english: 88:9 O Lord God of hosts, who is like to thee? * thou art mighty, O Lord, and thy truth is round about thee.

segments.t: Dómine, Deus virtútum, quis símilis tibi? * potens es, Dómine, et véritas tua in circúitu tuo.

content.latin: 88:10 Tu domináris potestáti maris: * motum autem flúctuum eius tu mítigas.
content.english: 88:10 Thou rulest the power of the sea: * and appeasest the motion of the waves thereof.

segments.t: Tu domináris potestáti maris: * motum autem flúctuum eius tu mítigas.

content.latin: 88:11 Tu humiliásti sicut vulnerátum, supérbum: * in brácchio virtútis tuæ dispersísti inimícos tuos.
content.english: 88:11 Thou hast humbled the proud one, as one that is slain: * with the arm of thy strength thou hast scattered thy enemies.

segments.t: Tu humiliásti sicut vulnerátum, supérbum: * in brácchio virtútis tuæ dispersísti inimícos tuos.

content.latin: 88:12 Tui sunt cæli, et tua est terra, orbem terræ et plenitúdinem eius tu fundásti: * aquilónem, et mare tu creásti.
content.english: 88:12 Thine are the heavens, and thine is the earth: the world and the fulness thereof thou hast founded: * the north and the sea thou hast created.

segments.t: Tui sunt cæli, et tua est terra, orbem terræ et plenitúdinem eius tu fundásti: * aquilónem, et mare tu creásti.

content.latin: 88:13 Thabor et Hermon in nómine tuo exsultábunt: * tuum brácchium cum poténtia.
content.english: 88:13 Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name: * thy arm is with might.

segments.t: Thabor et Hermon in nómine tuo exsultábunt: * tuum brácchium cum poténtia.

content.latin: 88:14 Firmétur manus tua, et exaltétur déxtera tua: * iustítia et iudícium præparátio sedis tuæ.
content.english: 88:14 Let thy hand be strengthened, and thy right hand exalted: * justice and judgment are the preparation of thy throne.

segments.t: Firmétur manus tua, et exaltétur déxtera tua: * iustítia et iudícium præparátio sedis tuæ.

content.latin: 88:15 Misericórdia et véritas præcédent fáciem tuam: * beátus pópulus, qui scit iubilatiónem.
content.english: 88:15 Mercy and truth shall go before thy face: * blessed is the people that knoweth jubilation.

segments.t: Misericórdia et véritas præcédent fáciem tuam: * beátus pópulus, qui scit iubilatiónem.

content.latin: 88:16 Dómine, in lúmine vultus tui ambulábunt, et in nómine tuo exsultábunt tota die: * et in iustítia tua exaltabúntur.
content.english: 88:16 They shall walk, O Lord, in the light of thy countenance: and in thy name they shall rejoice all the day, * and in thy justice they shall be exalted.

segments.t: Dómine, in lúmine vultus tui ambulábunt, et in nómine tuo exsultábunt tota die: * et in iustítia tua exaltabúntur.

content.latin: 88:18 Quóniam glória virtútis eórum tu es: * et in beneplácito tuo exaltábitur cornu nostrum.
content.english: 88:18 For thou art the glory of their strength: * and in thy good pleasure shall our horn be exalted.

segments.t: Quóniam glória virtútis eórum tu es: * et in beneplácito tuo exaltábitur cornu nostrum.

content.latin: 88:19 Quia Dómini est assúmptio nostra, * et Sancti Israël, regis nostri.
content.english: 88:19 For our protection is of the Lord, * and of our king the holy one of Israel.

segments.t: Quia Dómini est assúmptio nostra, * et Sancti Israël, regis nostri.

content.latin: 88:20 Tunc locútus es in visióne sanctis tuis, et dixísti: * Pósui adiutórium in poténte: et exaltávi eléctum de plebe mea.
content.english: 88:20 Then thou spokest in a vision to thy saints, and saidst: * I have laid help upon one that is mighty, and have exalted one chosen out of my people.

segments.t: Tunc locútus es in visióne sanctis tuis, et dixísti: * Pósui adiutórium in poténte: et exaltávi eléctum de plebe mea.

content.latin: 88:21 Invéni David, servum meum: * óleo sancto meo unxi eum.
content.english: 88:21 I have found David my servant: * with my holy oil I have anointed him.

segments.t: Invéni David, servum meum: * óleo sancto meo unxi eum.

content.latin: 88:22 Manus enim mea auxiliábitur ei: * et brácchium meum confortábit eum.
content.english: 88:22 For my hand shall help him: * and my arm shall strengthen him.

segments.t: Manus enim mea auxiliábitur ei: * et brácchium meum confortábit eum.

content.latin: 88:23 Nihil profíciet inimícus in eo, * et fílius iniquitátis non appónet nocére ei.
content.english: 88:23 The enemy shall have no advantage over him: * nor the son of iniquity have power to hurt him.

segments.t: Nihil profíciet inimícus in eo, * et fílius iniquitátis non appónet nocére ei.

content.latin: 88:24 Et concídam a fácie ipsíus inimícos eius: * et odiéntes eum in fugam convértam.
content.english: 88:24 And I will cut down his enemies before his face; * and them that hate him I will put to flight.

segments.t: Et concídam a fácie ipsíus inimícos eius: * et odiéntes eum in fugam convértam.

content.latin: 88:25 Et véritas mea, et misericórdia mea cum ipso: * et in nómine meo exaltábitur cornu eius.
content.english: 88:25 And my truth and my mercy shall be with him: * and in my name shall his horn be exalted.

segments.t: Et véritas mea, et misericórdia mea cum ipso: * et in nómine meo exaltábitur cornu eius.

content.latin: 88:26 Et ponam in mari manum eius: * et in flumínibus déxteram eius.
content.english: 88:26 And I will set his hand in the sea; * and his right hand in the rivers.

segments.t: Et ponam in mari manum eius: * et in flumínibus déxteram eius.

content.latin: 88:27 Ipse invocábit me: Pater meus es tu: * Deus meus, et suscéptor salútis meæ.
content.english: 88:27 He shall cry out to me: Thou art my father: * my God, and the support of my salvation.

segments.t: Ipse invocábit me: Pater meus es tu: * Deus meus, et suscéptor salútis meæ.

content.latin: 88:28 Et ego primogénitum ponam illum * excélsum præ régibus terræ.
content.english: 88:28 And I will make him my firstborn, * high above the kings of the earth.

segments.t: Et ego primogénitum ponam illum * excélsum præ régibus terræ.

content.latin: 88:29 In ætérnum servábo illi misericórdiam meam: * et testaméntum meum fidéle ipsi.
content.english: 88:29 I will keep my mercy for him for ever: * and my covenant faithful to him.

segments.t: In ætérnum servábo illi misericórdiam meam: * et testaméntum meum fidéle ipsi.

content.latin: 88:30 Et ponam in sǽculum sǽculi semen eius: * et thronum eius sicut dies cæli.

content.latin: Quid magnum fuit Regi sæculórum Regem fíeri hóminum? Non enim Rex Israël Christus ad exigéndum tribútum vel exércitum ferro armándum hostésque visibíliter debellándos; sed Rex Israël, quod mentes regat, quod in ætérnum cónsulat, quod in regnum cælórum credéntes, sperántes amantésque perdúcat. Dei ergo Fílius æquális Patri, Verbum per quod facta sunt ómnia, quod Rex esse vóluit Israël, dignátio est, non promótio; miseratiónis indícium est, non potestátis augméntum. Qui enim appellátus est in terra Rex Iudæórum, in cælis est Dóminus Angelórum. Sed Iudæórum tantum Rex est Christus, an et géntium? Immo et géntium. Cum enim dixísset in prophetía: Ego autem sum constitútus Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, prǽdicans præcéptum Dómini: ne propter montem Sion solis Iudǽis eum regem quisquam díceret constitútum, contínuo subiécit: Dóminus dixit ad me: Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te; póstula a me et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
content.english: What great matter was it for the King of all worlds to become King of men? For Christ was not King of Israel for exacting of tribute, or arming a host with the sword, and visibly subduing enemies: but King of Israel that he should rule minds, that he should counsel for eternity, that he should bring unto the kingdom of heaven them that believe, hope, and love. Being then, Son of God, the Word by whom all things were made, that it should be his will to be King of Israel is condescension, not preferment, a betokening of mercy, not an increasing of power. For he who was called on earth King of the Jews is in heaven Lord of the Angels. But is Christ King of the Jews only, or also King of the Gentiles? Yea, of the Gentiles also. For when he said in the prophecy: But I am set by him as King upon Sion his holy mountain, preaching the precepts of the Lord, lest on account of the Mount Sion, any should say that he was set as King only of the Jews, he hath straightway subjoined: The Lord hath said unto me, Thou art my Son: this day I have begotten thee. Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thy inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.

content.latin: Respóndit Iesus: Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo. Si ex hoc mundo esset regnum meum, minístri mei útique decertárent, ut non tráderer Iudǽis; nunc autem regnum meum non est hinc. Hoc est quod bonus Magíster scire nos vóluit; sed prius nobis demonstránda fúerat vana hóminum de regno eius opínio, sive géntium, sive Iudæórum a quibus id Pilátus audíerat: quasi proptérea morte fuísset plecténdus, quod illícitum affectáverit regnum, vel quóniam solent regnatúris invidére regnántes, et vidélicet cavéndum erat ne eius regnum sive Románis, sive Iudǽis esset advérsum.
content.english: Jesus answered: My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should be delivered to the Jews; but now is my kingdom not from hence. This it is which was the will of our Good Master that we should know: but first we were to be shown the vanity of the opinion concerning his kingdom, entertained by men, whether Gentiles or Jews, from whom Pilate had heard that: as if the reason why he must be punished by death, were that he had affected a kingdom to which he had no right; or because the reigning are wont to look with an evil eye upon those destined to reign; and there were indeed need to beware lest his kingdom should be adverse either to the Romans or the Jews.

content.latin: Póterat autem Dóminus quod ait, Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo, ad primam interrogatiónem prǽsidis respondére, ubi ei dixit, Tu es rex Iudæórum? sed eum vicíssim intérrogans, utrum hoc a semetípso díceret, an audísset ab áliis, illo respondénte osténdere vóluit hoc sibi apud illum fuísse a Iudǽis velut crimen obiéctum: patefáciens nobis cogitatiónes hóminum, quas ipse nóverat, quóniam vanæ sunt; eísque post responsiónem Piláti, iam Iudǽis et géntibus opportúnius aptiúsque respóndens, Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo.
content.english: Now the Lord might have answered at once: My kingdom is not from hence: to the first question put by the governor, Art thou the King of the Jews? But in putting a question in return, namely whether he spake this of himself, or had been told it by others, it was his will to show by Pilate's reply that this had been laid up to him as a crime by the Jews in their conference with the Governor: thus laying open to us, the thoughts of men, which he knew: that they are vain: and to them after Pilate's answer, making a reply which was more reasonable and suitable to Jews and Gentiles: My kingdom is not of this world.
